q-71776.name: Question 1
q-71776.worked_solution:
First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $2x.$ We can factor out the $2x$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{3}+14{x}^{2}+24x & =0 \\ 2x({x}^{2}+7x+12) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression ${x}^{2}+7x+12$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x({x}^{2}+7x+12) & =0 \\ 2x(x+4)(x+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $x=0,$ $x=-4,$ and $x=-3.$

Question 1
?

Solve the equation 2x3+14x2+24x=0.

a
x=0,3,4
b
x=−4,0,3
c
x=−4,−3,0
d
x=−3,0,8
e
x=−4,0,6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of 2x. We can factor out the 2x as follows: 2x3+14x2+24x=02x(x2+7x+12)=0

Now, we factor the expression x2+7x+12 as follows: 2x(x2+7x+12)=02x(x+4)(x+3)=0

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are x=0, x=−4, and x=−3.

q-70388.name: Question 2
q-70388.problem: Find the roots of the polynomial $p(y)=10{y}^{3}+5{y}^{2}-5y.$
q-70388.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(y)=0,$ that is

$$
10{y}^{3}+5{y}^{2}-5y=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $5y.$ We can factor out the $5y$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y(2{y}^{2}+y-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $2{y}^{2}+y-1$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5y(2{y}^{2}+y-1) & =0 \\ 5y(2y-1)(y+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $y=0,$ $y=\frac{1}{2},$ and $y=-1$

q-70389.name: Question 3
q-70389.worked_solution:
First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $4t.$ We can factor out the $4t$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{t}^{3}-20{t}^{2}+24t & =0 \\ 4t({t}^{2}-5t+6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression ${t}^{2}-5t+6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4t({t}^{2}-5t+6) & =0 \\ 4t(t-2)(t-3) & =0.\end{aligned}

q-37615.problem: Find the solutions of the equation $20{p}^{3}+7{p}^{2}=6p.$
q-37615.worked_solution:
First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form ${P}_{n}(p)=0.$ To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes $0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}20{p}^{3}+7{p}^{2} & =6p \\ 20{p}^{3}+7{p}^{2}-6p & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $p.$ We can factor out the $p$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}20{p}^{3}+7{p}^{2}-6p & =0 \\ p(20{p}^{2}+7p-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $20{p}^{2}+7p-6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(20{p}^{2}+7p-6) & =0 \\ p(5p-2)(4p+3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $p=0,$ $p=\frac{2}{5},$ and $p=-\frac{3}{4}.$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}12{s}^{3}+6{s}^{2}-36s & =0 \\ 6s(2{s}^{2}+s-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}6s(2{s}^{2}+s-6) & =0 \\ 6s(2s-3)(s+2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $s=0,$ $s=\frac{3}{2},$ and $s=-2.$

Question 10

Determine the real roots of the cubic equation 12s3+12s2−20s=6s2+16s.

a
s=−2,0,13
b
s=−2,0,32
c
s=−32,0,2
d
s=−2,0,1
e
s=0,2,32
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's rewrite the polynomial equation in the form Pn(s)=0. To do this, we subtract all the terms from the right-hand side so that the right-hand side becomes 0: 12s3+12s2−20s=6s2+16s12s3+6s2−20s=16s12s3+6s2−36s=0

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of 6s. We can factor out the 6s as follows: 12s3+6s2−36s=06s(2s2+s−6)=0

Now, we factor the expression 2s2+s−6 as follows: 6s(2s2+s−6)=06s(2s−3)(s+2)=0

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are s=0, s=32, and s=−2.

\begin{aligned}14{p}^{4}-10{p}^{3}+5{p}^{2} & =2{p}^{4}+17{p}^{2} \\ 12{p}^{4}-10{p}^{3}+5{p}^{2} & =17{p}^{2} \\ 12{p}^{4}-10{p}^{3}-12{p}^{2} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $2{p}^{2}.$ We can factor out the $2{p}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}12{p}^{4}-10{p}^{3}-12{p}^{2} & =0 \\ 2{p}^{2}(6{p}^{2}-5p-6) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $6{p}^{2}-5p-6$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{p}^{2}(6{p}^{2}-5p-6) & =0 \\ 2{p}^{2}(3p+2)(2p-3) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}15{w}^{4}(4{w}^{2}-7w+3) & =0 \\ 15{w}^{4}(4w-3)(w-1) & =0\end{aligned}

q-70467.worked_solution:
To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation $p(z)=0,$ that is

$$
18{z}^{4}+3{z}^{3}-3{z}^{2}=0.
$$

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of $3{z}^{2}.$ We can factor out the $3{z}^{2}$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{2}(6{z}^{2}+z-1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we factor the expression $6{z}^{2}+z-1$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}3{z}^{2}(6{z}^{2}+z-1) & =0 \\ 3{z}^{2}(3z-1)(2z+1) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are $z=0,$ $z=\frac{1}{3},$ and $z=-\frac{1}{2}.$

Find the roots of the polynomial p(z)=18z4+3z3−3z2.

a
z=−12,0,13
b
z=−32,0,1
c
z=−16,0,13
d
z=0,14,12
e
z=−12,1,43
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To find the roots of the polynomial, we must solve the equation p(z)=0, that is 18z4+3z3−3z2=0.

First, notice that all of the terms of the polynomial have a common factor of 3z2. We can factor out the 3z2 as follows: 3z2(6z2+z−1)=0

Now, we factor the expression 6z2+z−1 as follows: 3z2(6z2+z−1)=03z2(3z−1)(2z+1)=0

Finally, by applying the zero product rule, the solutions are z=0, z=13, and z=−12.
